Kitchen, meals & drinks

cutting board noun

also chopping board

modern

M-O

incīsōrium, incīsōriī n.

noun, second declension

By modern extension of a medieval trencher or carving board: Morgan–Owens traces incīsōrium to medieval dining and carving use. The modern chopping-board sense is an extension.

Examples

  • Mālum in incīsōriō secā.

    Cut the apple on the cutting board.composed

  • Hoc est incīsōrium; haec est rādula.

    This is the cutting board; this is the grater.composed

Other words

  • tabula secandī

    also used · our formation

    A transparent working alternative, used in Libellus IV.

See also kitchen knife, cheese grater, wood.

SourcesMorgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections
